dedupe_keys.name: recorded nnpc pipeline vandalism cases in nigeria january 2015 to january 2021 with covid 19 lockdown analysis tables

description: This Harvard Dataverse deposit by Nneka Onwuachi-Iheagwara supports a study of how pipeline vandalism on Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) pipelines changed under the COVID-19 lockdown movement restrictions. It uses recorded cases of pipeline vandalism from NNPC dated 1 January 2015 to 31 January 2021. The files are an original data table, ANOVA tables for COVID-19 groups and historical subgroups, time series analysis tables for the same groupings, a table for a six-month lockdown comparison, and a readme in text and Word form. The terms of use state a CC0 licence with additional terms, and the files are free to download. It was published in June 2021 and not updated since. Coverage is the NNPC pipeline network in Nigeria. Caveats: the records are case counts compiled by the corporation, not located incidents, the study is about one question, and the page does not describe fields in detail. Simulation uses are frequency of deliberate damage for sabotage exposure and resilience of oil product pipelines. Related records: data-gem-global-gas-infrastructure-tracker covers pipeline assets; no other energy record here holds vandalism counts.
